cases.name: Carrie Williams
cases.about: She was a student at Pittsburg State University.
cases.relationship: Classmate / student / teacher; Landlord / neighbor / roommate / tenant
cases.narrative:
He stabbed her 7 times through the heart, and her liver had been badly damaged, possibly by stomping. Her body was heavily bruised and her jaw was fractured. She also had a wound over her eyebrow that was caused by a sharp object. Socks tied to a chair in the bedroom, along with socks tied to her right leg, indicated that she had been tied to the chair at one point.   There was also evidence that she had been sodomized by some object, and there were body fluids on her shirt.

On several occasions prior to the murder, Carrie and her roommate, Robyn, had returned to the apartment to find the door open. In September 1995, money and Robyn's camera were stolen from the apartment. At the time it was stolen, the camera had contained film with photographs Robyn had taken on a trip to Padre Island, Texas. The camera also had sand in the viewfinder as the result of that trip. Carrie and Robyn requested that the lock to their apartment be changed as a result of the break-ins.

Carrie and Robyn had also been receiving obscene telephone calls from an unidentified male caller. The caller indicated that he knew their names and wished to engage in anal intercourse with Carrie. After Robyn reported the calls to police, Carrie's mother bought a caller identification unit for the apartment and the calls subsequently ceased.

Police discovered Kleypas' telephone number had registered on the caller ID in Carrie's apartment at 1:48 on the morning of the murder. One of the officers recognized the name and knew that Kleypas lived nearby and was on parole for a prior murder. A neighbor found a roll of film on the ground beside Kleypas' car on the morning of the murder. The developed roll contained photographs of Robyn and her friends and three photographs of the inside of Kleypas' apartment.

After his arrest, In the car, Kleypas admitted that he had killed Carrie. Kleypas told the officers that he had entered the front door after ringing the door bell. Carrie answered the door, and Kleypas forced his way in with a filet knife. He forced Carrie into her bedroom and tied her to a chair. When he attempted to tie her hands, she panicked. She told him that if he would leave she would give him a head start before calling police. After being told he had been identified on the caller ID, Kleypas admitted making the telephone calls to the apartment. He said that he had called the night prior to the murder but did not recall saying anything.

Once in Girard at the Crawford County Sheriff's Office, Kleypas agreed to give the officers further details. Kleypas said he first attempted to enter the apartment through the front window. He had taken the screen off and the window broke. He took the screen to a trash can in the alley and then went to the front door. When Kleypas rang the bell the first time, Carrie peered out and called out for Mike, her fiancee.   She said she knew it was Mike and said he should stop horsing around. She went back inside and Kleypas rang the bell again. When she answered, he forced himself inside. He said he might have slapped Carrie and that they ran into the couch in the living room. He forced her into the bedroom and made her undress. Kleypas used socks to bind Carrie. He attempted intercourse but was unable to obtain an erection. He said he penetrated her vaginally with his fingers. He also admitted that he had been watching C.W. and her roommate and had been making obscene telephone calls to them.

After he put his fingers into her vagina, Kleypas allowed Carrie to dress. She asked him to leave and said she would give him a head start. At some point, Carrie said she recognized him as the man who lived in the green house down the street. After he unplugged the telephone from the wall, there was a struggle because Carrie did not want her hands bound.

When Carrie became free of the chair, Kleypas tried to strangle her with his hands but that did not work. He took a piece of clothing and stuffed it into her mouth. When that was not successful, Kleypas found the knife and stabbed her repeatedly in the chest.  He then took the engagement ring from her finger and some of the contents from her purse and left the apartment. Kleypas said he later disposed of some of the clothing he wore that night and other items by dropping them into a dumpster at a Springfield car wash, but he was uncertain what happened to the ring and it was never found.

cases.name: Jase Elizabeth Delich
cases.about: Her obituary said, "Following graduation from Labette County High School this year, she attended Pittsburg School of Beauty. In July, she began working as a nail tech at Salon LA in Pittsburg. Her greatest enjoyment came from spending time with her family, especially her sister, Alyson. Known for being a goofball, Jase loved to make people laugh. She was artistic and enjoyed painting and was always up for an adventure. Jase’s big heart made her an avid rescuer of pets and people."
